supersedes.note: First-class Reasoning Profile concept. The 2026-09-23 rule that 'different effective reasoning controls become distinct profiles only when they change deployment behavior' is narrowed: when an effective SUPPORTED ON/OFF reasoning control exists, Reasoning On and Reasoning Off are both REQUIRED full WELP deployment profiles, never optional variants.

purpose: Qualify a model's actual reasoning topology experimentally BEFORE scored work and require the deployment profiles the model genuinely exposes. Motivated by ling-3.0-tiny: reasoning ON was the classified profile while enable_thinking=false was proven to produce effective OFF behavior that was never characterized, leaving the model's legitimate alternate deployment profile unknown.
scope_note: Determine EFFECTIVE behavior on the pinned runtime; the request field alone never qualifies a control. This contract changes which profiles must exist; it does not change any scoring contract, gate, fixture, or classification rule.

B.label: Reasoning present, cannot be disabled
B.meaning: Effective reasoning behavior exists but no supported effective OFF control exists (unavailable, ineffective, or unsupported on the pinned runtime).

C.label: Effective ON/OFF control exists
C.meaning: Both states are real and supported on the pinned runtime; each is experimentally proven, not assumed from the request field.

D.label: Additional effort levels exist
D.meaning: The base case (A, B, or C, recorded in base_case) is additionally accompanied by bounded reasoning-effort levels (low/medium/high/budget/effort/thinking depth). Effort levels are QUALIFIED prospectively and become full profiles only when genuinely supported, measurably distinct, deployment-relevant, and sufficient to change practical interpretation.
D.required_profiles: same as base_case, plus any effort level promoted under the effort-level policy

machine_profile_ids.reasoning-<level>: Reasoning <Level> — only for a qualified, promoted effort level (e.g. reasoning-high / Reasoning High)

qualification_record.case: A | B | C | D (case D additionally requires base_case A|B|C and additional_effort_levels)
qualification_record.controls: list of {control, requested_state, effective_state, evidence:{path, sha256}} — every examined reasoning control with its MEASURED effective behavior on the pinned runtime
qualification_record.off_control: {status: effective|unavailable|ineffective|unsupported, control, evidence:{path, sha256}} — status effective requires raw proof of OFF behavior (no reasoning channel) AND raw proof of the ON comparator from the same runtime; ineffective/unavailable/unsupported require the recorded attempt evidence
qualification_record.publisher_default_profile: standard | reasoning-on | reasoning-off | reasoning-<level> — the profile matching publisher/default deployment behavior; context only, never a demotion of the other supported profile(s)
qualification_record.additional_effort_levels: list of {level, control, qualification: {status: distinct_deployment_relevant|not_distinct|unqualified, evidence:{path, sha256}, measured_differences:{...}}} — present for case D; a level may become a full profile ONLY with status distinct_deployment_relevant

profile_requirements.full_profile: Each required profile is a complete WELP campaign event with its own profile identity, setup, calibration, response ceilings, prompt/control binding, reliability, safety, real-work results, context results, performance, evidence bundle, classification and deployment guidance. No diagnostic-only afterthought, no shared calibration, no ceiling reuse across profiles.
profile_requirements.same_task_set: Where applicable the SAME frozen model-agnostic task set is used across reasoning profiles so results are directly comparable; profile-specific setup/calibration may differ and must not alter fixture difficulty.
profile_requirements.independent_classification: Each profile gets its own derived classification. Averaging, merging, scoring or verbally collapsing distinct profile verdicts into one artificial model-level score is PROHIBITED. A model-level summary may state the publisher/default profile and the alternate supported profile(s) and provide deployment guidance; it must not flatten them.
profile_requirements.profile_invariant_evidence: Genuinely profile-invariant records (model source identity, license, artifact SHA-256, quant identity, architecture, runtime commit/build, physical hardware, pure load/fit qualification, unchanged template identity, artifact provenance) MAY be shared, but only when explicitly marked in manifest.profile_invariant_evidence with hash-bound references and provenance. Behavioral evidence (effective reasoning state, calibration, ceilings, scored outputs, reliability, safety outcomes, capability modules, context cells, generation performance, latency, token consumption, classification) is PROFILE-SPECIFIC and is never shared merely because artifact/runtime/hardware are identical.
profile_requirements.bound: Normal profile count: Standard model 1 profile; reasoning model without OFF 1 profile; reasoning model with effective OFF 2 profiles. Additional effort profiles are exceptional and prospectively justified. No unbounded configuration sweep and no post-hoc best-mode search.

manifest_binding.reasoning_topology: {contract: welp-reasoning-topology-0.1.0-draft, case, base_case (case D), off_control_status, publisher_default_profile, additional_effort_levels (case D), evidence:{path, sha256}} — hash-bound pointer to the frozen qualification record; required in new-era campaign manifests
manifest_binding.reasoning_profile: {profile, display_name, publisher_default (bool), group:{group_id, required_profiles, sibling_events:[{profile, event_id, state: complete|pending}]}} — this event's profile identity inside its reasoning group; case C groups list exactly the two required profiles
manifest_binding.profile_invariant_evidence: list of {kind, path, sha256, shared_across_profiles: true, note} — the ONLY evidence allowed to be shared across sibling profile events

reuse_policy.rules: Evidence reused from a prior event of the same model (e.g. a pre-reasoning-profiles campaign re-derived under the new snapshot) is legitimate only for the SAME effective reasoning profile, with explicit reuse provenance records ({class, source_event_id, source_path, source_sha256, rationale}) in the new event's evidence; behavioral evidence is reused only where the new methodology proves the underlying task, prompt, artifact, runtime, sampler, reasoning state, setup semantics and evidence format scientifically compatible. A reused classification is always re-derived under the new snapshot and validator-approved; it is never grandfathered.
reuse_policy.contamination: Evidence belonging to a different reasoning profile of the same model is NEVER reused as another profile's behavioral evidence. Cross-profile behavioral binding fails validation closed.

regression_contract: case A model yields exactly one Standard profile; case B yields Reasoning On with an explicit unavailable/ineffective/unsupported OFF record; case C yields both Reasoning On and Reasoning Off
a requested-but-ineffective OFF control never creates a Reasoning Off profile (no fake OFF)
case C sibling events share a group_id, carry independent classifications, and never average verdicts
cross-profile behavioral evidence binding is rejected; explicitly marked profile-invariant evidence is accepted
additional effort levels are qualified before promotion; unqualified levels never become full profiles
a case C model whose sibling profile event is still pending records an incomplete model characterization
historical one-profile events remain valid unchanged under their frozen snapshots
